'''Paige Cognetti''' (née '''Gebhardt'''; born August 27, 1980)<ref>{{cite web |last1=Burton |first1=Paul |date=November 6, 2019 |title=Cognetti becomes Scranton's first female mayor |url=https://www.bondbuyer.com/news/cognetti-becomes-scrantons-first-female-mayor |website=The Bond Buyer |language=en-US |access-date=October 20, 2026}}</ref> is an American politician serving since 2020 as [[List of mayors of Scranton, Pennsylvania|mayor of Scranton]], [[Pennsylvania]]. She is the first woman to be mayor of the city and won her seat in a special election.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Heller |first=karen |date=July 23, 2020 |title=Scranton became shorthand for the past. Its reality is far more complicated. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/scranton-became-shorthand-for-the-past-its-reality-is-far-more-complicated/2020/07/21/f15b56a6-c76b-11ea-8ffe-372be8d82298_story.html |website=The Washington Post |issn=0190-8286 |language=en-US |access-date=May 17, 2021}}</ref><ref name="CNN">{{Cite news |last1=Cole |first1=Devan |date=November 6, 2019 |title=First woman elected mayor of Scranton, as an independent after sparring with Democratic machine |url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/11/06/politics/scranton-pennsylvania-mayor-paige-cognetti-democrat-independent/index.html |work=CNN |language=en-US |access-date=May 17, 2021}}</ref> A member of the Democratic Party, she ran her first Scranton mayoral campaign as an independent. She is the Democratic nominee for [[Pennsylvania's 8th congressional district]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Horvath |first1=Jeff |date=June 15, 2026 |title=Cognetti campaign opens office in Scranton |url=https://www.thetimes-tribune.com/2026/06/15/cognetti-campaign-opens-office-in-scranton/ |website=Scranton Times-Tribune |language=en-US |access-date=June 17, 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Cognetti was born in [[Eugene, Oregon]]. She graduated ''[[summa cum laude]]'' from the [[University of Oregon]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in English literature and Romance languages, and earned a [[Master of Business Administration]] from [[Harvard Business School]].{{cn|date=September 2025}}

After graduating, she worked as an English teacher in Japan through the [[JET Programme]].<ref name="LinkedIn">{{cite web |last1=Cognetti |first1=Paige |title=Cognetti's LinkedIn profile |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/paigegebhardtcognetti/ |website=LinkedIn |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=April 13, 2026}}</ref> She was a fundraiser for [[Hillary Clinton]]'s and [[Barack Obama]]'s 2008 presidential campaigns and served as an advisor at the [[U.S. Department of the Treasury]] in Obama's first term.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mayor of Scranton to Deliver Johnson College's 2020 Commencement Address |url=https://johnson.edu/2020/03/mayor-of-scranton-to-deliver-johnson-colleges-2020-commencement-address/ |website=Johnson College of Technology |language=en-US |date=March 11, 2020 |access-date=May 19, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Wiesner |first1=Ashley Lorraine |date=June 9, 2020 |title=Now the mayor of Scranton, PA, Paige Gebhardt Cognetti's passion for equity inspired by her time in CHC |url=https://honors.uoregon.edu/now-mayor-scranton-pa-paige-gebhardt-cognettis-passion-equity-inspired-her-time-chc |website=Clark Honors College |language=en |access-date=May 17, 2021}}</ref>

Cognetti was appointed to the [[Scranton School District (Pennsylvania)|Scranton School Board]] in 2017,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Buynovsky |first1=Sarah |title=Paige Cognetti Named First Female Mayor of Scranton |url=https://www.wnep.com/article/news/local/lackawanna-county/paige-cognetti-named-first-female-mayor-of-scranton/523-faf7f7fd-0042-405d-95de-ea88e5b34f55 |work=WNEP-TV |date=November 5, 2019 |access-date=February 29, 2024}}</ref> but resigned in December 2018 to become a special assistant to Pennsylvania's state auditor, [[Eugene DePasquale]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Krawczeniuk |first1=Borys |last2=Kelly |first2=Christopher J. |date=December 12, 2018 |title=Cognetti Resigns From Scranton School Board To Work For State Auditor General |url=https://apnews.com/article/cc6d493175254d9eafe243bcade61c6c |website=Associated Press |language=en-US |access-date=May 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210519052628/https://apnews.com/article/cc6d493175254d9eafe243bcade61c6c |archive-date=May 19, 2021 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> While serving on the board, she criticized no-bid school bus contracts and unapproved payments to contractors.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Hofius Hall |first1=Sarah |date=May 14, 2021 |title=Scranton School Board To Ask District Attorney To Investigate Mechanic Insurance |url=https://apnews.com/article/scranton-school-boards-f1e2a5d571c445368f317c474655523c |website=Associated Press |language=en-US |access-date=May 19, 2021}}</ref>

==Mayor of Scranton==
=== Elections ===
Cognetti ran in the 2019 special election to finish the term of [[Scranton]] mayor [[Bill Courtright]], who had pleaded guilty to corruption charges earlier that year.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lange |first1=Stacy |date=January 6, 2020 |title=Paige Cognetti Sworn In as Scranton's First Female Mayor |url=https://www.wnep.com/article/news/local/lackawanna-county/paige-cognetti-sworn-in-as-scrantons-first-female-mayor/523-3afb7c6b-d7fa-49a3-9cca-358d1b4e5471 |work=WNEP-TV |language=en-US |access-date=October 2, 2022}}</ref> She ran as an independent after she deemed the local Democratic Party's closed caucus system undemocratic. Her campaign emphasized investments in local businesses, education, and infrastructure.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 15, 2019 |title=Scranton Mayor-Elect Paige Cognetti offers an object lesson for Philly politics |url=https://thephiladelphiacitizen.org/wheres-our-paige-against-the-machine/ |website=The Philadelphia Citizen |language=en-US |access-date=May 19, 2021}}</ref> She won the special election with 36% of the vote.<ref name=CNN /> 

In 2021, Cognetti ran as a Democrat for a full term and defeated her Republican opponent, 72.5% to 23.4%.<ref name="Lange 2021-11-03">{{cite news |last1=Lange |first1=Stacy |date=November 3, 2021 |title=Mayor Paige Cognetti has declared victory in Scranton |url=https://www.wnep.com/article/news/local/lackawanna-county/mayor-paige-cognetti-has-declared-victory-in-scranton/523-b46cc216-b218-4323-a124-b2b7ff048216 |work=WNEP-TV |language=en-US |access-date=October 2, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=December 3, 2021 |title=2021GeneralSummary_Certified.pdf |url=https://cms8.revize.com/revize/lackawanna/Document_center/Government/Department/Elections/Election%20result/MUNICIPAL%20ELECTION%20NOVEMBER%202%202021/2021GeneralSummary_Certified.pdf |website=[[Lackawanna County, PA]] |page=22 |language=en-US |access-date=August 21, 2022}}</ref>

=== Tenure ===
During Cognetti's tenure as mayor, Scranton completed its exit from [[Financially Distressed Municipalities Act|Pennsylvania's Act 47]] financial distress program and improved its bond rating, allowing the city to reduce reliance on short-term borrowing.<ref name="Horvath 2025-03-25">{{Cite web |last1=Horvath |first1=Jeff |date=March 25, 2025 |title='Unlock the future': Cognetti touts achievements in optimistic state of the city address |url=https://www.thetimes-tribune.com/2025/03/25/unlock-the-future-cognetti-touts-achievements-in-optimistic-state-of-the-city-address/ |website=Scranton Times-Tribune |language=en-US |access-date=June 17, 2026}}</ref> Her administration undertook infrastructure and public works projects, including investments in stormwater systems and parks, demolition of hazardous structures, and upgrades to municipal signage.<ref name="Horvath 2025-03-25"/>

The city's housing stock expanded, while the administration implemented initiatives to modernize municipal operations and improve service efficiency.<ref name="Culkin 2026-04-22">{{Cite news |last=Culkin |first=Jack |date=April 22, 2026 |title=Mayor Cognetti highlights Scranton's revival, goals in State of the City address |url=https://www.wnep.com/article/news/local/lackawanna-county/mayor-cognetti-highlights-scrantons-revival-goals-in-state-of-the-city-address-paige-progress/523-d64e7b23-ba67-4df4-ac39-ad924ecf50ec |work=ABC WNEP (Channel 16) |language=en-US |access-date=June 16, 2026}}</ref> Downtown redevelopment also continued during this period, accompanied by increased construction activity across the city.<ref name="Culkin 2026-04-22"/>

In 2024, President [[Joe Biden]] appointed Cognetti to the [[United States Trade Representative]]'s Advisory Committee for Trade Policy and Negotiations.<ref>{{cite news |date=February 23, 2024 |title=President Biden appoints Scranton Mayor Cognetti as a member of the Advisory Committee |url=https://www.wnep.com/article/news/local/lackawanna-county/president-biden-appoints-scranton-mayor-cognetti-as-a-member-of-the-advisory-committee-lackawanna-county/523-d968588f-b5ca-4306-8854-9959c31d9a07 |work=WNEP-TV |access-date=February 29, 2024}}</ref>

== 2026 U.S. House campaign ==
On September 2, 2025, Cognetti announced her candidacy for [[Pennsylvania's 8th congressional district]] in [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania#District 8|2026]], aiming to unseat Republican incumbent Representative [[Rob Bresnahan]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Svirnovskiy |first1=Gregory |date=September 2, 2025 |title=Scranton mayor launches House campaign, goes after Rob Bresnahan's stock trades |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/09/02/paige-cognetti-scranton-mayor-rob-bresnahan-congress-race-00539390 |work=Politico |language=en-US |access-date=September 7, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Terruso |first1=Julia |date=September 2, 2025 |title=Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti launches run for Congress, blasting Rep. Rob Bresnahan's stock trading |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/paige-cognetti-congress-rob-bresnahan-scranton-20250902.html |website=The Philadelphia Inquirer |language=en-US |access-date=September 2, 2025}}</ref> Cognetti ran on an [[anti-corruption]] platform, criticizing Bresnahan for his stock trading since becoming a member of Congress.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McIntire |first1=Mary Ellen |date=October 13, 2026 |title=Democrat bets on anti-corruption pitch in Pennsylvania swing district |url=https://rollcall.com/2026/10/13/pennsylvania-battleground-election-paige-cognetti-bresnahan/ |website=Roll Call |language=en-US |access-date=October 20, 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
She is married to Ryan Cognetti and has two children.<ref name="Lange 2021-11-03"/><ref>{{cite web |title=About the Mayor |url=https://scrantonpa.gov/your-government/mayor-2/about-the/ |website=ScrantonPa.gov |access-date=February 28, 2024}}</ref>
